headline: Mostly dry, warm Saturday, then a strong cold front Saturday night brings damaging wind risk, heavy rain bursts, and high surf Sunday.
summary: Showers are fading tonight after a front moved east of the Cascades, with lows in the 40s. Saturday should be mostly dry across western Washington into the afternoon, with highs in the 60s, though rain may linger at times on the western Olympic Peninsula. A stronger cold front arrives Saturday evening and moves through Saturday night, bringing a burst of steadier rain, briefly 0.15 to 0.25 inch per hour along the front. Strong south wind is the bigger concern. Forecasters give a 50 to 75% chance of gusts above 58 mph (the High Wind Warning threshold) on the coast, where a High Wind Watch is in effect. Most other areas can expect gusts of 30 to 45 mph from Saturday evening into early Sunday. Many trees still have leaves, so localized power outages are possible, and clogged storm drains are possible where wind and steady rain overlap Saturday evening, so allow extra travel time. Sunday brings showers, mostly over the North Cascades and Olympics, with snow levels (the elevation where rain turns to snow) dropping from about 7,500 feet to near 4,500 feet, so snow is limited to high mountain areas. Highs cool into the 50s. Attention turns to the coast, where seas of 20 to 28 feet will produce large breaking waves. A High Surf Advisory is in effect from 4 AM to 10 PM Sunday and could be upgraded to a warning. Be especially careful if digging razor clams. More rain, milder temperatures, and breezy conditions follow from Monday afternoon through midweek, with more widespread rain late in the week. Forecasters are fairly confident in the Saturday night windstorm but not certain how strong the gusts will get, and said more wind alerts may be needed elsewhere. Uncertainty grows from Wednesday on.
changes: The evening discussion changed little. It added that more wind alerts may be needed outside the coast, dropped the earlier Wind Advisory and Gale Warning now that the first front has passed, and noted the High Surf Advisory could be upgraded to a warning.
